listBibl.bibl: Felix Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, vol. 1 (Halle: Niemeyer, 1903), p. 620

An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: Ps Cn for Prol
div.ab: He sunt sanctiones de foresta, quas ego Canutus rex, cum consilio primariorum hominum meorum de foresta, condo et facio, ut cunctis regni nostri Anglie ecclesiis et pax et iustitia fiat, et ut omnis delinquens rite secundum modum delicti et delinquentis fortunam patiatur.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 620 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: These are the ordinances concerning the forest which I, King Cnut, with the counsel of my chief men, make and enact concerning the forest, so that both peace and justice may be done to all the churches of our realm of England, and so that every offender may duly suffer according to the manner of the offence and the fortune of the offender.
